source_refs.note: Topic 2.6.2, printed page 33: the p orbitals (Figure 2.6).

blocks.text: The electron density of a 2p orbital is not distributed in a spherically symmetric way as in an s orbital. Instead a p orbital has two lobes on one of the axes. The three p orbitals are named px, py and pz according to their axes.

blocks.prompt: There are three orientations of the p orbital because of three values of the magnetic quantum number. Justify this.
blocks.explanation: For a p subshell l = 1, so m takes the 2l + 1 = 3 values -1, 0 and +1. Each value is one orientation in space, and the three orbitals are the two-lobed px, py and pz lying along the three perpendicular axes.

items: A p orbital has two lobes along an axis; px, py and pz lie along the three axes, one for each value of m.
